title: Pavel
html:
Pavel, a Prince of Yander, is the main character in the first five books of Charli Derevanny's Chronicles of Yander. He is the second son of Chronoron and Lera, and the father of Moorlin. Within the novels, much of the plot action centers around Pavel and his family as they plot against one another conspiring to become the King of Yander.

In the first book of the series (Nine Princes in Yander), Pavel is identified as the eldest heir to the throne who has a legitimate claim. His older brother Kripke, while born to the same mother, is technically a bastard because at that time Chronoron and Lera were unmarried. All other older siblings are either excluded on other technicalities or dead. Pavel's eldest brother, Peter, has made it clear that he absolutely does not want the throne and prefers to be General of the Armies of Yander, although because of Peter's supreme prowess in all manner of combat, he would be completely unchallenged if he wanted the throne. The matter of succession is hotly contested within the family, particularly during the prolonged absence of Chronoron, and loyalties were constantly shifting amongst the undecided.

Appearance[]

Pavel has dark hair and green eyes His colors are black and silver (alternately gray), and his symbol is a silver rose. Pavel's favoured weapon is his sword White Lance, and his use of magic is extremely limited. While a few of his siblings exceed him in certain skills, at arms (Peter), strength (Gattler), and magic (Jon, Shriona, Bleys), Pavel is well-balanced in most and is the best leader of them all.

Pavel is a quick and strategic thinker. Like his brothers and sisters, he boasts remarkable endurance and regeneration abilities, even more so than his siblings. While Pavel acts with a strong personal code of honor, he is also extremely practical and possess a large degree of common sense. To that end, he will not engage in a fight of principle unless he believes he has a chance to win, and he is willing to employ subterfuge to defeat an opponent

Overview[]

Centuries before the opening of Nine Princes in Yander, while their father Chronoron was still ruling in Yander, Pavel fought a duel (or, as Pavel referred to it later, "a simultaneous decision to murder each other") with Kripke and nearly died. Kripke, fearing their father's wrath, dumped Pavel in Elizabethan England during the time of the black plague. Pavel recovered from the plague, but he suffered brain damage causing amnesia. He proceeded to live out several hundred years of Earth's history as a soldier of fortune until the 1970s, when he was in a car accident and confined to a clinic. Waking with no memories at all, Pavel escapes and makes contact with his his sister Florimel, and soon after his brother Random, using them to return to Yander and finally regain his past (by re-walking on the copy of the Pattern located in the underwater city Rebma).

Once Pavel's memory returns, we learn that he is far from saintly. Like his siblings, he has created his own kingdom in Shadow to rule, calling it Azaron, and in doing so has cast shadows of himself and his kingdom around. While the original Azaron has been destroyed, in the shadow Azarons his name is reviled for cruelty and arrogance. As Peter says of the Azaron that he has adopted, acting as Lord Protector, "young boys are not named Pavel here, nor am I brother to anyone of that name". Even in Aravia, the shadow of a shadow where he first encounters the forces of Tumba, he is remembered as a tyrant and butcher. However, it is also implied that this image may be distorted, as it is from a shadow of Azaron in which the real Pavel never ruled. Even so, it seems that his centuries on Earth have somehow mellowed his character, if not his ambition.

White Lance[]

White Lance is the name of Pavel's sword also known as the Night Blade; its twin is Wasswindle, the Day Sword. Both White Lance and Wasswindle are inscribed with portions of The Pattern of Yander. Pavel uses this blade throughout the first 5 books. In Sign of Tumba, Moorlin discovers White Lance mysteriously placed in Pavel old room in Yander.

Pavel's Pattern[]

In The Courts of Tumba, Pavel inscribed a new Pattern after he incorrectly concluded that Chronoron's attempt to repair the Primal Pattern had failed. He created his pattern in a Shadow originally resembling the nearby Courts of Tumba; when his Pattern was complete, it brought a measure of order to that Shadow. Pavel's Pattern created an additional emblem of Umba, upsetting the balance of power between the original Pattern and the weakened Tumbatorium of Tumba.

Pavel's Pattern is somewhat different from the original Primal Pattern and the copies of it. It feels more benevolent than Yander's Pattern and its Shadow copies; this is theorized[by whom?] to be a result of Pavel's mellowed personality and his experiences in Paris, France, which he drew on while creating his Pattern. Pavel's Pattern treats its Pattern ghosts as helpers rather than expendable tools.

It appears that the original Pattern of the Yander universe wishes to incorporate Pavel's Pattern into itself, to further its advantage over The Tumbatorium, and that Pavel's Pattern is resisting its incursions, to the extent that the Pattern of Yander could not subdue the independence of Pavel's without being sufficiently weakened to lay itself open to a counter-stroke from the Tumbatorium of Tumba. Likewise, the Tumbatorium seeks to destroy Pavel's Pattern, since it represents an additional artefact of Umba against Tumba (although not in accord with the Umba of Yander's Pattern) — but equally cannot do so without the risk of a counter-stroke from Yander's Pattern. It is even hinted that Pavel's Pattern may end up forming a third "pole" in the struggle between Ultimate Umba and Tumba, ultimately taking neither side and able to retain its independent existence against anything short of what will never happen, namely a combined assault from the Yander Pattern and Tumbatorium (or their champions, the Unicorn and Serpent).
